title: CV Tutorial: original-source checks for chapters 26–28
scope: Original method mechanisms, code/documentation contracts and reproducible illustrative tests; experiments are not benchmark reproductions.

entries.claim: SimCLR uses two independently augmented views per image, 2N views per batch, and NT-Xent with self-similarity excluded
entries.notes: Positive denotes same image instance, not same semantic class.

entries.claim: Nonlinear projection head is applied between encoder representation and contrastive loss, while downstream evaluation often uses encoder features
entries.notes: Do not compare projected features with unprojected pretrained features without noting this choice.

entries.claim: MoCo uses a queue of negative keys and a momentum-updated key encoder to maintain a consistent large dictionary
entries.notes: Queue is the original MoCo variant; later versions change recipes.

entries.claim: DINO uses cross-view student/teacher self-distillation with EMA, centering and sharpening to prevent representation collapse
entries.notes: Teacher target is stopped-gradient; avoid characterizing as vanilla contrastive loss.

entries.claim: Original DINOv2 models were pretrained on approximately 142 million curated, unlabeled images
entries.notes: Scale is a historical project property, not an SSL prerequisite.

entries.claim: DINOv2 extends self-distillation with a recipe including image-level and patch-level objectives
entries.notes: Claim describes design family; code examples show only the core teacher-student relationship.

entries.claim: MAE masks a high patch ratio (typically 75 percent) and feeds only visible patches to heavy encoder, inserting mask tokens in lightweight decoder
entries.notes: Toy experiment checks patch counts only, not image reconstruction benchmarks.

entries.claim: CLIP trains image and text encoders on paired data using a symmetric image-to-text and text-to-image contrastive objective
entries.notes: Zero-shot inference requires specifying class descriptions and prompt templates.

entries.claim: Original CLIP work describes training on 400 million internet image-text pairs
entries.notes: Historical data property; not a generic requirement.

entries.claim: BLIP introduces caption filtering and multimodal understanding/generation pretraining
entries.notes: Unlike CLIP, not merely a dual embedding similarity model.

entries.claim: LLaVA connects a visual encoder to a language model using a projector and visual instruction tuning
entries.notes: Generates text responses rather than direct symmetric image-text similarities.

entries.claim: DDPM uses Gaussian forward noising; x_t can be sampled directly using cumulative alpha and standard Gaussian epsilon
entries.notes: Toy script verifies q(x_t|x_0) with a simple synthetic tensor.

entries.claim: Simplified epsilon-prediction MSE is one common DDPM training objective, not the complete reverse sampling algorithm
entries.notes: Sampling also depends on schedule and posterior parameterization.

entries.claim: Latent Diffusion Models perform denoising in compressed autoencoder latent space and use cross-attention for conditioning
entries.notes: Latent autoencoder is lossy; cannot conflate with pixel-space DDPM.

entries.claim: NeRF models a continuous view-dependent radiance field with volume rendering along camera rays
entries.notes: Original view synthesis uses calibrated multi-view input.

entries.claim: 3D Gaussian Splatting optimizes explicit anisotropic Gaussians and visibility-aware rasterization for novel-view rendering
entries.notes: Real-time claim is configuration-specific; no universal FPS is asserted.

entries.claim: Group-aware data splitting prevents the same identified group appearing in both train and test folds
entries.notes: User must identify the leakage group appropriate for their domain.

entries.claim: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss expects unnormalized logits and class-index targets for standard multiclass classification
entries.notes: Toy demo uses [N,2] and integer class indices.

entries.claim: PyTorch seed settings and deterministic algorithms improve reproducibility but do not guarantee identical results across hardware and versions
entries.notes: DataLoader worker-specific RNG handling also matters.

entries.claim: Saving and loading state_dict via weights_only semantics is a safer portable model-weight workflow than loading untrusted full-object pickles
entries.notes: Checkpoint still needs model architecture, preprocessing and label map.

entries.claim: Macro F1 averages per-class F1 equally, while overall accuracy can hide minority class failures
entries.notes: Business threshold must come from measured costs and validation data.

entries.claim: Operational AI requires governance and risk management beyond offline benchmark scores
entries.notes: This is risk management guidance, not proof of any deployment safety guarantee.
